title: AI regulation deadlines
disclaimer: Operational information, not legal advice. Check the linked source before relying on a row.

items.title: AI disclosure duties in Utah
items.applies_to: Businesses using generative AI with Utah consumers, with stricter duties in regulated professions
items.summary: Disclose the use of generative AI on request in consumer interactions and proactively in regulated professions.
items.evidence: Disclosure texts, script for staff answering 'am I talking to AI?'.

items.title: AI literacy duty, Article 4
items.applies_to: Providers and deployers of AI systems
items.summary: Take measures to support the development of AI literacy of staff and others who operate or use AI on your behalf. The Digital Omnibus (July 2026) replaced the earlier duty to ensure, to your best extent, a sufficient level: no specific level has to be guaranteed and no certificate is required. The duty itself was kept, and national authorities supervise it.
items.evidence: An internal record of trainings and other measures (training register), the training programme and written AI usage rules; a short check of learning is good practice.
items.source_label: European Commission, AI literacy Q&A (updated 27 July 2026)

items.title: Prohibited AI practices, Article 5
items.applies_to: Providers and deployers of AI systems
items.summary: Eight practices are banned: harmful manipulation and deception, exploiting vulnerabilities, social scoring, predicting crime from profiling alone, untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion recognition at work and in education (except for medical or safety reasons), biometric categorisation that infers sensitive characteristics, and real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement, with narrow exceptions. Fines up to 35 million euro or 7% of worldwide annual turnover. The Commission's guidelines include recruitment in the workplace emotion ban.
items.evidence: Classification record showing that no system falls under Article 5; acceptable use policy that forbids the banned uses; vendors' written confirmation for tools with emotion or biometric features.

items.title: General-purpose AI model obligations
items.applies_to: Providers of general-purpose AI models only
items.summary: Technical documentation, copyright policy and a training-data summary for model providers, with extra duties for models with systemic risk. Companies that only use AI tools are not in scope.
items.evidence: Not applicable to deployers.

items.title: Generative AI training-data documentation
items.applies_to: Developers of generative AI systems made available to Californians
items.summary: Developers must publish documentation about the datasets used to train their generative AI.
items.evidence: Published training-data summary (developers only).

items.title: TRAIGA in force
items.applies_to: Developers and deployers of AI in Texas; state agencies
items.summary: Bans intentional development or deployment of AI that incites self-harm or crime, AI-generated child sexual abuse material, non-consensual deepfake pornography and government social scoring. Rules for state-government AI.
items.evidence: Acceptable-use policy prohibiting the banned uses.
items.source_label: King & Spalding, state AI laws effective 1 Jan 2026

items.title: AI Basic Act in force
items.applies_to: Domestic and foreign AI developers and businesses using AI in products; foreign firms above revenue or user thresholds must appoint a Korean representative
items.summary: Generative AI providers must notify users that AI is used and label AI-generated content, with clear notice where generated audio, image or video is hard to tell from real. One-year grace period before administrative fines, except serious cases.
items.evidence: User notices and labels on generative outputs, domestic representative if thresholds met.
items.source_label: Cooley, Korea AI Basic Act overview

items.title: High-impact AI obligations activated
items.applies_to: Operators of high-impact AI (healthcare, energy, transport, hiring, biometric analysis and similar)
items.summary: Impact assessment on fundamental rights before deployment, meaningful explanation of outcomes, human oversight, a user protection plan and documentation. Fines up to KRW 30 million for notification failures, missing representative or refusing inspection.
items.evidence: Impact assessment record, oversight design, user protection plan.
items.source_label: Cooley, Korea AI Basic Act overview

items.title: Transparency obligations, Article 50
items.applies_to: Providers of AI that talks to people or generates content; deployers of emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deepfakes and AI-written public-interest text
items.summary: Chatbots must disclose they are AI unless obvious. Generated audio, image, video and text must be marked as artificial in a machine-readable way. Deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest text must be disclosed. Disclosure must be clear and given at the latest at first interaction. Not deferred by the Omnibus.
items.evidence: Disclosure texts in place, marking mechanism documented, transparency checklist completed per system.

items.title: Provenance and detection tools for large generative AI providers
items.applies_to: Providers of generative image, video or audio tools with more than 1 million monthly users
items.summary: Offer AI detection tools, watermark options and disclosures for AI-generated content. Delayed from 1 January 2026 to 2 August 2026.
items.evidence: Provenance features and disclosure options (large providers only).

items.title: Polish AI Systems Act, main provisions in force
items.applies_to: Companies and public bodies operating in Poland
items.summary: National law implementing the EU AI Act. Creates KRiBSI (Komisja Rozwoju i Bezpieczeństwa Sztucznej Inteligencji) as supervisor, a binding individual-opinion procedure (150 PLN fee, 30 to 60 days) and a regulatory sandbox that is free for SMEs.
items.evidence: Register of AI systems, assigned roles, AI usage policy, vendor commitments.

items.title: KRiBSI inspections and fines begin
items.applies_to: Companies and public bodies operating in Poland
items.summary: KRiBSI may inspect on 7 days' notice, remotely by default, covering documentation, procedures, internal logs, cloud systems and contractor agreements, and may impose the AI Act fine tiers. For SMEs the cap is the lower of the fixed amount and the percentage of turnover.
items.evidence: Inspection protocol, named contact, document index, trade-secret marking.

items.law: EU AI Act as amended by Reg. 2026/1744
items.title: Machine-readable marking of generative AI output
items.applies_to: Providers of generative AI systems and, in practice, companies publishing generated content
items.summary: New obligation introduced by the Digital Omnibus: generated output must carry machine-readable marking. The same package bans generating non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material, with penalties up to €35M or 7% of global turnover.
items.evidence: Marking mechanism in place for every generative system in the inventory.

items.title: Provenance duties extend to large online platforms
items.applies_to: Large online platforms (2027) and capture-device manufacturers (2028)
items.summary: Extends SB 942 obligations to platforms from 1 January 2027 and to capture devices from 1 January 2028.
items.evidence: Platform provenance handling (platforms only).

items.title: ADMT significant-decision obligations
items.applies_to: Businesses under the CCPA using automated decision-making for significant decisions about consumers
items.summary: Notices, opt-out and access rights around automated decisions with significant effects.
items.evidence: ADMT notice, opt-out process, risk assessment where required.

items.title: Colorado ADMT duties begin
items.applies_to: Developers and deployers of automated decision-making technology affecting Colorado consumers
items.summary: Replaces the 2024 Colorado AI Act. Requires pre-use consumer notices, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, meaningful human review rights and developer documentation. The earlier risk-management-programme and impact-assessment duties were removed.
items.evidence: Pre-use notice texts, adverse-outcome explanation procedure, human review process.

items.title: Frontier-model developer duties
items.applies_to: Developers of frontier AI models only (trained with more than 10^26 operations); stricter duties for large frontier developers with annual revenue above $500 million
items.summary: Transparency and reporting on training, deployment, safety protocols and incidents for frontier developers. The chapter amendment signed 27 March 2026 takes effect on 1 January 2027 and sets civil penalties of up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations. Not relevant to companies that only use AI.
items.evidence: Not applicable to deployers.

items.title: End of the one-year grace period for fines (expected)
items.applies_to: All businesses in scope of the Act
items.summary: The grace period on administrative fines runs at least one year from 22 January 2026. Treat this date as the earliest point at which routine fines start.
items.evidence: All generative-AI notices and high-impact assessments complete.
items.source_label: Cooley, Korea AI Basic Act overview

items.law: EU AI Act as amended by Reg. 2026/1744
items.title: High-risk obligations for stand-alone systems (Annex III)
items.applies_to: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI in employment, education, credit, essential services, law enforcement, migration and justice
items.summary: Risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, human oversight, conformity assessment and registration. Deferred from 2 August 2026 by the Digital Omnibus.
items.evidence: Risk classification record, impact assessment, vendor documentation, oversight design.

items.law: EU AI Act as amended by Reg. 2026/1744
items.title: High-risk obligations for AI in regulated products (Annex I)
items.applies_to: AI embedded in products under EU product law (machinery, medical devices, vehicles and similar)
items.summary: Deferred from 2 August 2027 by the Digital Omnibus.
items.evidence: Product conformity files updated for AI components.
